title: The Letter of Bellwether Lane Anew
premise: Quentin Joubert, a night dispatcher for Bellwether Taxi with a reputation for closing every case she takes, is hired by a nervous woman named Ada Voss to prove that a murder on the waterfront hasn't happened yet — a murder foretold in an anonymous letter dated three days in the future. When the predicted victim turns up alive and then vanishes, Quentin discovers the letter echoes one written eleven years ago, tied to a drowning the police ruled accidental and her own estranged brother helped bury. Following the tide charts, the old letters, and the taxi company's ledgers, she uncovers a cover-up protected by the people who raised her. In the end Quentin must choose between exposing the truth — which destroys her brother and the found family at the depot — or letting the sea keep its secret; she chooses truth, closes the case no one wanted reopened, and loses the family she built to gain the justice she couldn't refuse.
about_author: Silas Voss is the pen name of a former harbor-town journalist who spent a decade covering cold cases along the northern coast before turning to fiction. They write at night, they claim, because that's when the town tells the truth.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A rain-soaked night shift; a stranger named Ada Voss pays triple rate to hire Bellwether Taxi to prove a murder hasn't happened yet, producing a letter that names a victim and a date three days out. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into unease as Quentin realizes the letter describes the depot's own address.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Fares
chapters.summary: Quentin checks dispatch logs against the letter's details and finds a fare booked for the named victim, dockworker Tomas Reyes, on the predicted night. POV alternates between Quentin and a brief Ada interlude revealing she received the letter anonymously. Beat: dread disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: Tomas Reyes, Alive
chapters.summary: Quentin tracks Reyes to a boarding house and finds him frightened but breathing, insisting he's being followed by someone who smells of engine oil and salt. First-person tension: Quentin can't decide if this is a hoax or a countdown. Beat: the case becomes personal when Reyes mentions her brother's name.

chapters.title: What My Brother Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Quentin's POV: eleven years ago, her brother Marius was a rookie cop on the drowning case of a girl named Lira Halden, ruled accidental. Quentin remembers the night he came home soaked and silent. Beat: guilt surfacing like something the tide returns.

chapters.title: Night Two
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The second letter arrives, correcting the first: the murder will happen, just not to whom it said. Ada and Quentin compare handwriting and realize both letters are written on Bellwether Taxi trip carbon paper. Beat: paranoia inside the only place Quentin feels safe.

chapters.title: The Depot Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter from Quentin's POV introducing the night crew — dispatcher Odile, mechanic Bram, driver Sef — whose loyalty has been her real family since Marius left. Someone altered the logbook. Beat: warmth shadowed by the first crack of betrayal.

chapters.title: Reyes Vanishes
chapters.summary: Quentin arrives to move Reyes to safety and finds his room scrubbed clean, tide charts pinned to the wall with dates circled. The third letter is waiting under her own door. Beat: fear hardening into resolve; the hunter realizes she is also prey.

chapters.title: Lira Halden Did Not Drown
chapters.summary: Investigative chapter: Quentin pulls the old coroner's file and finds the autopsy contradicts the ruling — Lira had defensive bruises. Marius signed off under pressure from then-Sergeant Corvel, now the harbor captain. Beat: righteous anger with nowhere legal to put it.

chapters.title: Corvel's Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts Captain Corvel at the harbor office; he is courteous, menacing, and offers her money to drop it. She notices the same engine-oil-and-salt smell Reyes described. Beat: the law revealed as part of the crime.

chapters.title: Sef Drives at Night
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He confesses partially: he's been driving Corvel's men on 'quiet fares' for years, believing he was protecting the depot from ruin. He swears he never knew what the fares carried. Beat: loyalty vs. truth tearing him in half.

chapters.title: The Fourth Letter
chapters.summary: The fourth letter names its author's intended confession date and location: the old pilot house on Bellwether Lane, at high tide. Quentin deduces the letters are written by someone dying or planning to die. Beat: pity braided with suspicion — the letter-writer may be the killer seeking absolution.

chapters.title: Ada's Secret
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Quentin confronts her about inconsistencies in her story and learns Ada is Lira Halden's older sister, returned after years abroad, who wrote the first letter herself based on a deathbed note from their mother. Beat: the client becomes a co-conspirator; trust rebuilt on shared grief.

chapters.title: Bram's Hands
chapters.summary: Quentin searches the garage and finds Bram repairing a boat engine with parts matching Corvel's launch — the boat used the night Lira died. Bram begs her to stop, saying Marius took the fall once already. Beat: the found family fractures openly.

chapters.title: Marius Comes Home
chapters.summary: Marius appears at the depot, hollowed out, claiming he's been receiving the same letters and came back to stop the writer before Corvel does. Sibling confrontation: years of silence, blame, and love. Beat: love against duty, both siblings armed with truths the other can't bear.

chapters.title: Reyes Found
chapters.summary: Fishermen pull Tomas Reyes alive from a channel buoy; he confirms Corvel's men held him to find out who'd hired the taxis. Quentin realizes the letters' true target was always the cover-up, and every warning was a lure. Beat: relief sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Odile Knew
chapters.summary: Odile confesses she recognized the handwriting weeks ago — it belongs to dying dispatcher Wim, founder of the depot, who drove the original 'fare' the night Lira died and has been mailing confessions no one would print. Beat: betrayal and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: High Water Rising
chapters.summary: Storm front moves in; tide charts show the highest water in eleven years, enough to uncover the weighted evidence in the channel. Corvel moves to destroy it tonight. Quentin, Ada, and Marius plan to reach the pilot house first. Beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Pilot House
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Quentin and Marius reach Wim at the pilot house as Corvel's men arrive. Wim, oxygen tank beside him, hands over the full confession and the ledger of quiet fares. Standoff in the storm. Beat: courage without any guarantee.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Climax resolves: Corvel himself comes for the ledger; Marius stands between them and finally testifies aloud to what he buried. Sef and Bram arrive with the depot's drivers as witnesses — the whole night shift choosing truth over survival. Corvel is taken by state investigators tipped by Ada. Beat: justice outside the law, won by outnumbering it.

chapters.title: Wim's Last Fare
chapters.summary: Wim dies at dawn asking Quentin to drive him past Bellwether Lane one last time in a Bellwether cab. She does, meter running, and lets the ride be free. Beat: mourning folded into mercy; the case closed the only way she knows how.

chapters.title: Closed Cases
chapters.summary: Aftermath: official reopening of the Halden case, Marius surrendering his pension and facing charges, Ada staying on as the depot's day dispatcher. Quentin reads the final letter, which thanks her for taking a case no one else would close. Beat: bittersweet restoration.

chapters.title: Bellwether Lane, Anew
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Quentin's POV, one year later. A new client pays in advance for an impossible job; Quentin smiles, takes it, and dispatches the first cab of the night. The lane, the tide, and the depot endure. Beat: renewal — the promise that some cases are worth losing everything for.
